activities.3.2.2.14: beta-nicotinamide D-ribonucleotide + H2O = D-ribose 5-phosphate + nicotinamide + H(+).
activities.3.2.2.15: Hydrolyzes DNA and polynucleotides, releasing free hypoxanthine.
activities.3.2.2.17: Cleaves the N-glycosidic bond between the 5'-pyrimidine residue in cyclobutadipyrimidine (in DNA) and the corresponding deoxy-D-ribose residue.
activities.3.2.2.19: (1) N(omega)-(ADP-D-ribosyl)-L-arginyl-[protein] + H2O = ADP-D-ribose + L-arginyl-[protein]. (2) N(omega)-(ADP-D-ribosyl)-L-arginine + H2O = ADP-D-ribose + L-arginine.
activities.3.2.2.21: Hydrolysis of alkylated DNA, releasing 3-methyladenine, 3-methylguanine, 7-methylguanine and 7-methyladenine.
activities.3.2.2.22: Endohydrolysis of the N-glycosidic bond at one specific adenosine on the 28S rRNA.
activities.3.2.2.23: Hydrolysis of DNA containing ring-opened 7-methylguanine residues, releasing 2,6-diamino-4-hydroxy-5-(N-methyl)formamidopyrimidine.
activities.3.2.2.27: Hydrolyzes single-stranded DNA or mismatched double-stranded DNA and polynucleotides, releasing free uracil.
activities.3.2.2.28: Specifically hydrolyzes mismatched double-stranded DNA and polynucleotides, releasing free uracil.
activities.3.2.2.29: Hydrolyzes mismatched double-stranded DNA and polynucleotides, releasing free thymine.
activities.3.2.2.31: Hydrolyzes free adenine bases from 7,8-dihydro-8-oxoguanine:adenine mismatched double-stranded DNA, leaving an apurinic site.
activities.3.3.2.2: (1) a 1-O-(1Z-alkenyl)-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine + H2O = a 2,3- saturated aldehyde + sn-glycerol 3-phosphocholine. (2) a 1-O-(1Z-alkenyl)-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine + H2O = a 2,3- saturated aldehyde + sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine.
activities.3.4.11.1: Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Xaa-|-Yaa-, in which Xaa is preferably Leu, but may be other amino acids including Pro although not Arg or Lys, and Yaa may be Pro. Amino acid amides and methyl esters are also readily hydrolyzed, but rates on arylamides are exceedingly low.
activities.3.4.11.2: Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Xaa-|-Yaa- from a peptide, amide or arylamide. Xaa is preferably Ala, but may be most amino acids including Pro (slow action). When a terminal hydrophobic residue is followed by a prolyl residue, the two may be released as an intact Xaa-Pro dipeptide.
activities.3.4.11.3: Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Cys-|-Xaa-, in which the half- cystine residue is involved in a disulfide loop, notably in oxytocin or vasopressin. Hydrolysis rates on a range of aminoacyl arylamides exceed that for the cystinyl derivative, however.
activities.3.4.11.4: Release of the N-terminal residue from a tripeptide.
activities.3.4.11.5: Release of N-terminal proline from a peptide.
activities.3.4.11.6: Release of N-terminal Arg and Lys from oligopeptides when P1' is not Pro. Also acts on arylamides of Arg and Lys.
activities.3.4.11.7: Release of N-terminal glutamate (and to a lesser extent aspartate) from a peptide.
activities.3.4.11.9: Release of any N-terminal amino acid, including proline, that is linked to proline, even from a dipeptide or tripeptide.
activities.3.4.11.10: Release of an N-terminal amino acid, preferentially leucine, but not glutamic or aspartic acids.
activities.3.4.11.13: Release of any N-terminal amino acid, including proline and hydroxyproline, but no cleavage of Xaa-|-Pro.
activities.3.4.11.14: Release of an N-terminal amino acid, preferentially alanine, from a wide range of peptides, amides and arylamides.
activities.3.4.11.16: Release of a variety of N-terminal residues (especially glutamate and leucine) from peptides, provided tryptophan (or at least phenylalanine or tyrosine) is the penultimate residue. Also acts on Glu-|-Trp, Leu-|-Trp and a number of other dipeptides.
activities.3.4.11.17: an N-terminal L-tryptophanyl-L-alpha-aminoacyl-[peptide] + H2O = an N-terminal L-alpha-aminoacyl-[peptide] + L-tryptophan.
activities.3.4.11.18: Release of N-terminal amino acids, preferentially methionine, from peptides and arylamides.
activities.3.4.11.19: Release of an N-terminal D-amino acid from a peptide, Xaa-|-Yaa-, in which Xaa is preferably D-Ala, D-Ser or D-Thr. D-amino acid amides and methyl esters also are hydrolyzed, as is glycine amide.
activities.3.4.11.20: Differs from other aminopeptidases in broad specificity for amino acids in the P1 position and the ability to hydrolyze peptides of four or five residues that contain Pro in the P1' position.
activities.3.4.11.21: Release of an N-terminal aspartate or glutamate from a peptide, with a preference for aspartate.
activities.3.4.11.22: Release of an N-terminal amino acid, preferably a neutral or hydrophobic one, from a polypeptide. Aminoacyl-arylamides are poor substrates.
activities.3.4.11.23: Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Xaa, from a peptide or arylamide. Xaa is preferably Glu or Asp but may be other amino acids, including Leu, Met, His, Cys and Gln.
activities.3.4.11.24: Release of an N-terminal amino acid with a preference for large hydrophobic amino-terminus residues.
activities.3.4.11.25: Cleaves N-terminal beta-homoamino acids from peptides composed of 2 to 6 amino acids.
activities.3.4.11.26: The enzyme cleaves the 36-Pro-Pro-37 bond of cysteine desulfurase (EC 2.8.1.7) removing three amino acid residues (Tyr-Ser-Pro) from the N-terminus after cleavage by mitochondrial processing peptidase.
activities.3.4.11.27: an N-terminal L-arginyl-L-aminoacyl-[protein] + H2O = an N-terminal L-alpha-aminoacyl-[protein] + L-arginine.
activities.3.4.13.4: (1) beta-alanyl-L-lysine + H2O = beta-alanine + L-lysine. (2) beta-alanyl-L-ornithine + H2O = beta-alanine + L-ornithine. (3) beta-alanyl-L-arginine + H2O = beta-alanine + L-arginine. (4) N(2)-(4-aminobutanoyl)-L-lysine + H2O = 4-aminobutanoate + L-lysine. (5) N(2)-(4-aminobutanoyl)-L-ornithine + H2O = 4-aminobutanoate + L-ornithine. (6) N(2)-(4-aminobutanoyl)-L-arginine + H2O = 4-aminobutanoate + L-arginine.
activities.3.4.13.5: Hydrolysis of anserine (beta-alanyl-|-N(pi)-methyl-L-histidine), carnosine, homocarnosine, glycyl-|-leucine and other dipeptides with broad specificity.
activities.3.4.13.9: Xaa-L-Pro dipeptide + H2O = an L-alpha-amino acid + L-proline.
activities.3.4.13.17: Hydrolysis of dipeptides containing either D- or L-amino acids or both.
activities.3.4.13.18: Hydrolysis of dipeptides, preferentially hydrophobic dipeptides including prolyl amino acids.
activities.3.4.13.19: an L-aminoacyl-L-amino acid + H2O = 2 an L-alpha-amino acid.
activities.3.4.13.20: Preferential hydrolysis of the beta-Ala-|-His dipeptide (carnosine), and also anserine, Xaa-|-His dipeptides and other dipeptides including homocarnosine.
activities.3.4.13.21: Dipeptidase E catalyzes the hydrolysis of dipeptides Asp-|-Xaa. It does not act on peptides with N-terminal Glu, Asn or Gln, nor does it cleave isoaspartyl peptides.
activities.3.4.13.23: an S-substituted L-cysteinylglycine + H2O = an S-substituted L-cysteine + glycine.
activities.3.4.14.1: Release of an N-terminal dipeptide, Xaa-Yaa-|-Zaa-, except when Xaa is Arg or Lys, or Yaa or Zaa is Pro.
activities.3.4.14.2: Release of an N-terminal dipeptide, Xaa-Yaa-|-, preferentially when Yaa is Ala or Pro. Substrates are oligopeptides, preferentially tripeptides.
activities.3.4.14.4: Release of an N-terminal dipeptide from a peptide comprising four or more residues, with broad specificity. Also acts on dipeptidyl 2-naphthylamides.
activities.3.4.14.5: Release of an N-terminal dipeptide, Xaa-Yaa-|-Zaa-, from a polypeptide, preferentially when Yaa is Pro, provided Zaa is neither Pro nor hydroxyproline.
activities.3.4.14.6: Preferential release of dipeptides from a tetrapeptide, e.g. Ala- Gly-|-Ala-Gly. Acts more slowly on Ala-Ala-|-Ala-Ala and Gly-Gly-|-Gly- Gly.
activities.3.4.14.9: Release of an N-terminal tripeptide from a polypeptide, but also has endopeptidase activity.
activities.3.4.14.10: Release of an N-terminal tripeptide from a polypeptide.
activities.3.4.14.11: Hydrolyzes Xaa-Pro-|- bonds to release unblocked, N-terminal dipeptides from substrates including Ala-Pro-|-p-nitroanilide and (sequentially) Tyr-Pro-|-Phe-Pro-|-Gly-Pro-|-Ile.
activities.3.4.14.12: Hydrolysis of Xaa-Xaa-Pro-|-Yaa- releasing the N-terminal tripeptide of a peptide with Pro as the third residue (position P1) and where Yaa is not proline.
activities.3.4.14.13: The enzyme releases L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu dipeptides from cell wall peptides via cleavage of an L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu-|-L-Lys bond.
activities.3.4.14.14: [mycofactocin precursor peptide]-C-terminal glycyl-N- {5-[(4-hydroxyphenyl)methyl]-4,4-dimethyl-2-oxopyrrolidin-3-yl}acetamide + H2O = [mycofactocin precursor peptide]-C-terminal glycine + 3-amino-5- [(4-hydroxyphenyl)methyl]-4,4-dimethyl-2-pyrrolidin-2-one.
activities.3.4.15.1: Release of a C-terminal dipeptide, oligopeptide-|-Xaa-Yaa, when Xaa is not Pro, and Yaa is neither Asp nor Glu. Thus, conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, with increase in vasoconstrictor activity, but no action on angiotensin II.
activities.3.4.15.4: Release of a C-terminal dipeptide or exceptionally a tripeptide.
activities.3.4.15.5: Hydrolysis of unblocked, C-terminal dipeptides from oligopeptides, with broad specificity. Does not hydrolyze bonds in which P1' is Pro, or both P1 and P1' are Gly.
activities.3.4.16.2: Cleavage of a -Pro-|-Xaa bond to release a C-terminal amino acid.
activities.3.4.16.4: Preferential cleavage: (Ac)2-L-Lys-D-Ala-|-D-Ala. Also transpeptidation of peptidyl-alanyl moieties that are N-acyl substituents of D-alanine.
activities.3.4.16.5: Release of a C-terminal amino acid with broad specificity.
activities.3.4.16.6: Preferential release of a C-terminal arginine or lysine residue.
activities.3.4.17.1: Release of a C-terminal amino acid, but little or no action with -Asp, -Glu, -Arg, -Lys or -Pro.
activities.3.4.17.2: Preferential release of a C-terminal lysine or arginine amino acid.
activities.3.4.17.3: Release of a C-terminal basic amino acid, preferentially lysine.
activities.3.4.17.4: Release of a C-terminal amino acid from a peptide in which glycine is the penultimate amino acid, e.g. Z-Gly-|-Leu.
activities.3.4.17.6: Release of a C-terminal alanine from a peptide or a variety of pteroyl or acyl groups.
activities.3.4.17.10: Release of C-terminal arginine or lysine residues from polypeptides.
activities.3.4.17.11: Release of C-terminal glutamate residues from a wide range of N-acylating moieties, including peptidyl, aminoacyl, benzoyl, benzyloxycarbonyl, folyl and pteroyl groups.
activities.3.4.17.12: Cleavage of C-terminal arginine or lysine residues from polypeptides.
activities.3.4.17.15: Similar to that of carboxypeptidase A (EC 3.4.17.1), but with a preference for bulkier C-terminal residues.
activities.3.4.17.16: Release of a C-terminal residue other than proline, by preferential cleavage of a prolyl bond.
activities.3.4.17.18: Releases a C-terminal residue, which may be hydrophobic or positively charged.
activities.3.4.17.19: Release of a C-terminal amino acid with broad specificity, except for -Pro.
activities.3.4.17.20: Release of C-terminal Arg and Lys from a polypeptide.
activities.3.4.17.21: Release of an unsubstituted, C-terminal glutamyl residue, typically from Ac-Asp-Glu or folylpoly-gamma-glutamates.
activities.3.4.17.22: Releases C-terminal Arg and Lys from polypeptides.
activities.3.4.17.24: (1) C-terminal L-alpha-aminoacyl-L-glutamyl-L-glutamyl-[tubulin] + H2O = C-terminal L-alpha-aminoacyl-L-glutamyl-[tubulin] + L-glutamate. (2) C-terminal L-alpha-aminoacyl-L-glutamyl-[tubulin] + H2O = C-terminal L-alpha-aminoacyl-[tubulin] + L-glutamate.
activities.3.4.17.25: an S-substituted glutathione + H2O = S-substituted gamma-glutamyl-L- cysteine + glycine.
activities.3.4.18.1: Release of C-terminal amino acid residues with broad specificity, but lacks action on C-terminal proline. Shows weak endopeptidase activity.
activities.3.4.19.1: (1) Cleavage of an N-acetyl or N-formyl amino acid from the N-terminus of a polypeptide. (2) Internal cleavage of oxidized and glycated proteins.
activities.3.4.19.2: Cleavage of C-terminal glycinamide from polypeptides.
activities.3.4.19.3: Release of an N-terminal pyroglutamyl group from a polypeptide, the second amino acid generally not being Pro.
activities.3.4.19.5: Cleavage of a beta-linked Asp residue from the N-terminus of a polypeptide.
activities.3.4.19.6: Release of the N-terminal pyroglutamyl group from pGlu-|-His-Xaa tripeptides and pGlu-|-His-Xaa-Gly tetrapeptides.
activities.3.4.19.7: Release of an N-terminal, formyl-methionyl residue from a polypeptide.
activities.3.4.19.11: Hydrolysis of gamma-D-glutamyl bonds to the L-terminus (position 7) of meso-diaminopimelic acid (meso-A2pm) in 7-(L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu)-meso-A2pm and 7-(L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu)-7-(D-Ala)-meso-A2pm. It is required that the D-terminal amino and carboxy groups of meso-A2pm are unsubstituted.
activities.3.4.19.12: Thiol-dependent hydrolysis of ester, thioester, amide, peptide and isopeptide bonds formed by the C-terminal Gly of ubiquitin (a 76-residue protein attached to proteins as an intracellular targeting signal).
activities.3.4.19.13: (1) glutathione + H2O = L-cysteinylglycine + L-glutamate. (2) an S-substituted glutathione + H2O = an S-substituted L-cysteinylglycine + L-glutamate.
activities.3.4.19.14: leukotriene C4 + H2O = leukotriene D4 + L-glutamate.
activities.3.4.19.15: an N(6)-[small archaeal modifier protein]-[protein]-L-lysine + H2O = a [protein]-L-lysine + a [small archaeal modifier protein].
activities.3.4.19.16: (1) an S-[(1E)-1-(hydroxyimino)-omega-(methylsulfanyl)alkyl]-L- glutathione + H2O = an S-[(1E)-1-(hydroxyimino)-omega- (methylsulfanyl)alkyl]-L-cysteinylglycine + L-glutamate. (2) (E)-1-(glutathione-S-yl)-2-(1H-indol-3-yl)acetohydroximate + H2O = (E)-1-(glycyl-L-cystein-S-yl)-2-(1H-indol-3-yl)acetohydroximate + L-glutamate. (3) 2-(glutathion-S-yl)-2-(1H-indol-3-yl)acetonitrile + H2O = 2-(glycyl- L-cystein-S-yl)-2-(1H-indol-3-yl)acetonitrile + L-glutamate. (4) (Z)-1-(glutathione-S-yl)-2-phenylacetohydroximate + H2O = (Z)-1- (glycyl-L-cystein-S-yl)-2-phenylacetohydroximate + L-glutamate.
activities.3.4.21.1: Preferential cleavage: Tyr-|-Xaa, Trp-|-Xaa, Phe-|-Xaa, Leu-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.21.2: Preferential cleavage: Leu-|-Xaa, Tyr-|-Xaa, Phe-|-Xaa, Met-|-Xaa, Trp-|-Xaa, Gln-|-Xaa, Asn-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.21.3: Preferential cleavage: Tyr-|-Xaa, Phe-|-Xaa, Leu-|-Xaa. Little action on Trp-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.21.5: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Gly bonds in fibrinogen to form fibrin and release fibrinopeptides A and B.
activities.3.4.21.6: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Thr and then Arg-|-Ile bonds in prothrombin to form thrombin.
activities.3.4.21.7: Preferential cleavage: Lys-|-Xaa > Arg-|-Xaa, higher selectivity than trypsin. Converts fibrin into soluble products.
activities.3.4.21.9: Activation of trypsinogen by selective cleavage of 6-Lys-|-Ile-7 bond.
activities.3.4.21.12: Preferential cleavage: Ala-|-Xaa, Val-|-Xaa in bacterial cell walls, elastin and other proteins.
activities.3.4.21.21: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Ile bond in factor X to form factor Xa.
activities.3.4.21.22: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Ile bond in factor X to form factor Xa.
activities.3.4.21.25: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity.
activities.3.4.21.26: Hydrolysis of Pro-|-Xaa >> Ala-|-Xaa in oligopeptides.
activities.3.4.21.27: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Ala and Arg-|-Val bonds in factor IX to form factor IXa.
activities.3.4.21.32: Hydrolysis of proteins, with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Native collagen is cleaved about 75% of the length of the molecule from the N-terminus. Low activity on small molecule substrates of both trypsin and chymotrypsin.
activities.3.4.21.34: Cleaves selectively Arg-|-Xaa and Lys-|-Xaa bonds, including Lys-|-Arg and Arg-|-Ser bonds in (human) kininogen to release bradykinin.
activities.3.4.21.35: Preferential cleavage of Arg-|-Xaa bonds in small molecule substrates. Highly selective action to release kallidin (lysyl-bradykinin) from kininogen involves hydrolysis of Met-|-Xaa or Leu-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.21.36: Hydrolysis of proteins, including elastin. Preferential cleavage: Ala-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.21.37: Hydrolysis of proteins, including elastin. Preferential cleavage: Val-|-Xaa > Ala-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.21.38: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Ile bonds in factor VII to form factor VIIa and factor XI to form factor XIa.
activities.3.4.21.39: Preferential cleavage: Phe-|-Xaa > Tyr-|-Xaa > Trp-|-Xaa > Leu-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.21.41: Selective cleavage of Lys(or Arg)-|-Ile bond in complement subcomponent C1s to form the active form of C1s (EC 3.4.21.42).
activities.3.4.21.42: Cleavage of Arg-|-Ala bond in complement component C4 to form C4a and C4b, and Lys(or Arg)-|-Lys bond in complement component C2 to form C2a and C2b: the 'classical' pathway C3 convertase.
activities.3.4.21.43: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Ser bond in complement component C3 alpha- chain to form C3a and C3b, and Arg-|-Xaa bond in complement component C5 alpha-chain to form C5a and C5b.
activities.3.4.21.45: Inactivates complement subcomponents C3b, iC3b and C4b by proteolytic cleavage.
activities.3.4.21.46: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Lys bond in complement factor B when in complex with complement subcomponent C3b or with cobra venom factor.
activities.3.4.21.47: Cleavage of Arg-|-Ser bond in complement component C3 alpha-chain to yield C3a and C3b, and Arg-|-Xaa bond in complement component C5 alpha- chain to yield C5a and C5b.
activities.3.4.21.48: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity, and of Bz-Arg-OEt > Ac-Tyr-OEt. Does not hydrolyze peptide amides.
activities.3.4.21.49: Hydrolysis of proteins including native collagen at Xaa-|-Ala bond leaving an N-terminal (75%) and a C-terminal (25%) fragment.
activities.3.4.21.53: Hydrolysis of proteins in presence of ATP.
activities.3.4.21.54: Cleavage of the Leu-|-Leu bond in synthetic tetradecapeptide renin substrate, to produce angiotensin I, but not active on natural angiotensinogen. Also hydrolyzes Bz-Arg-p-nitroanilide.
activities.3.4.21.55: Preferential cleavage: Arg-|-Xaa bonds in fibrinogen to form fibrin and release fibrinopeptides A and B.
activities.3.4.21.57: Hydrolysis of proteins. Preferential cleavage: Leu-|-Xaa in small molecule substrates.
activities.3.4.21.59: Preferential cleavage: Arg-|-Xaa, Lys-|-Xaa, but with more restricted specificity than trypsin.
activities.3.4.21.60: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Thr and Arg-|-Ile in prothrombin to form thrombin and two inactive fragments.
activities.3.4.21.61: Cleavage of -Lys-Arg-|-Xaa- and -Arg-Arg-|-Xaa- bonds to process yeast alpha-factor pheromone and killer toxin precursors.
activities.3.4.21.62: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds, and a preference for a large uncharged residue in P1. Hydrolyzes peptide amides.
activities.3.4.21.63: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity, and of Bz-Arg-OEt > Ac-Tyr-OEt. Does not hydrolyze peptide amides.
activities.3.4.21.64: Hydrolysis of keratin, and of other proteins with subtilisin-like specificity. Hydrolyzes peptide amides.
activities.3.4.21.65: Rather non-specific hydrolysis of proteins. Preferential cleavage: -Ala-|-Xaa-, -Tyr-|-Xaa-, -Phe-|-Xaa- in small molecular substrates.
activities.3.4.21.67: Hydrolysis of proteins, but not Bz-Tyr-OEt, Ac-Phe-beta-naphthylester, or Bz-Arg-OEt.
activities.3.4.21.68: Specific cleavage of Arg-|-Val bond in plasminogen to form plasmin.
activities.3.4.21.69: Degradation of blood coagulation factors Va and VIIIa.
activities.3.4.21.70: Preferential cleavage: Ala-|-Xaa. Does not hydrolyze elastin.
activities.3.4.21.71: Preferential cleavage: Leu-|-Xaa, Met-|-Xaa and Phe-|-Xaa. Hydrolyzes elastin.
activities.3.4.21.72: Cleavage of immunoglobulin A molecules at certain Pro-|-Xaa bonds in the hinge region. No small molecule substrates are known.
activities.3.4.21.73: Specific cleavage of Arg-|-Val bond in plasminogen to form plasmin.
activities.3.4.21.74: Selective cleavage of Arg-|-Xaa bond in fibrinogen, to form fibrin, and release fibrinopeptide A. The specificity of further degradation of fibrinogen varies with species origin of the enzyme.
activities.3.4.21.75: Release of mature proteins from their proproteins by cleavage of -Arg- Xaa-Yaa-Arg-|-Zaa- bonds, where Xaa can be any amino acid and Yaa is Arg or Lys. Releases albumin, complement component C3 and von Willebrand factor from their respective precursors.
activities.3.4.21.76: Hydrolysis of proteins, including elastin, by preferential cleavage: -Ala-|-Xaa- > -Val-|-Xaa-.
activities.3.4.21.78: Hydrolysis of proteins, including fibronectin, type IV collagen and nucleolin. Preferential cleavage: -Arg-|-Xaa-, -Lys-|-Xaa- >> -Phe-|- Xaa- in small molecule substrates.
activities.3.4.21.80: Hydrolysis of proteins with specificity similar to chymotrypsin.
activities.3.4.21.81: Hydrolysis of proteins with trypsin-like specificity.
activities.3.4.21.82: Preferential cleavage: -Glu-|-Xaa- >> -Asp-|-Xaa-. Preference for Pro or Leu at P2 and Phe at P3. Cleavage of -Glu-|-Asp- and -Glu-|-Pro- bonds is slow.
activities.3.4.21.83: Hydrolysis of -Arg-|-Xaa- and -Lys-|-Xaa- bonds in oligopeptides, even when P1' residue is proline.
activities.3.4.21.84: Selective cleavage of 103-Arg-|-Ser-104 and 124-Ile-|-Ile-125 bonds in Limulus clotting factor B to form activated factor B. Cleavage of -Pro- Arg-|-Xaa- bonds in synthetic substrates.
activities.3.4.21.85: Selective cleavage of 98-Arg-|-Ile-99 bond in Limulus proclotting enzyme to form active clotting enzyme.
activities.3.4.21.86: Selective cleavage of 18-Arg-|- and 47-Arg-|- bonds in coagulogen to form coagulin and fragments.
activities.3.4.21.88: Hydrolysis of Ala-|-Gly bond in repressor LexA.
activities.3.4.21.89: Cleavage of hydrophobic, N-terminal signal or leader sequences from secreted and periplasmic proteins.
activities.3.4.21.90: Autocatalytic release of the core protein from the N-terminus of the togavirus structural polyprotein by hydrolysis of a -Trp-|-Ser- bond.
activities.3.4.21.91: Selective hydrolysis of -Xaa-Xaa-|-Yaa- bonds in which each of the Xaa can be either Arg or Lys and Yaa can be either Ser or Ala.
activities.3.4.21.92: Hydrolysis of proteins to small peptides in the presence of ATP and magnesium. alpha-casein is the usual test substrate. In the absence of ATP, only oligopeptides shorter than five residues are hydrolyzed (such as succinyl-Leu-Tyr-|-NHMec, and Leu-Tyr-Leu-|-Tyr-Trp, in which cleavage of the -Tyr-|-Leu- and -Tyr-|-Trp bonds also occurs).
activities.3.4.21.93: Release of protein hormones, neuropeptides and renin from their precursors, generally by hydrolysis of -Lys-Arg-|- bonds.
activities.3.4.21.94: Release of protein hormones and neuropeptides from their precursors, generally by hydrolysis of -Lys-Arg-|- bonds.
activities.3.4.21.95: Fully activates human clotting factor V by a single cleavage at the 1545- Trp-Tyr-Leu-Arg-|-Ser-Asn-Asn-Gly-1552 bond. Cattle, but not rabbit, factor V is cleaved, and no other proteins of the clotting system are attacked. Esterase activity is observed on Bz-Arg-OEt and Tos-Arg-OMe, and amidase activity on Phe-pipecolyl-Arg-NHPhNO2.
activities.3.4.21.96: Endopeptidase activity with very broad specificity, although some subsite preference have been noted, e.g. large hydrophobic residues in the P1 and P4 positions, and Pro in the P2 position. Best known for its action on caseins, although it has been shown to hydrolyze hemoglobin and oxidized insulin B-chain.
activities.3.4.21.97: Cleaves -Ala-|-Ser- and -Ala-|-Ala- bonds in the scaffold protein.
activities.3.4.21.98: Hydrolysis of four peptide bonds in the viral precursor polyprotein, commonly with Asp or Glu in the P6 position, Cys or Thr in P1 and Ser or Ala in P1'.
activities.3.4.21.99: Hydrolyzes arginyl bonds, preferably with Pro in the P2 position.
activities.3.4.21.100: Hydrolysis of the B chain of insulin at 13-Glu-|-Ala-14, 15-Leu-|-Tyr-16 and 25-Phe-|-Tyr-26 and angiotensin I at 4-Tyr-|-Ile-5. A good synthetic substrate is Lys-Pro-Ile-Glu-Phe-|-Phe(NO2)-Arg-Leu.
activities.3.4.21.102: The enzyme shows specific recognition of a C-terminal tripeptide, Xaa- Yaa-Zaa, in which Xaa is preferably Ala or Leu, Yaa is preferably Ala or Tyr, and Zaa is preferably Ala, but then cleaves at a variable distance from the C-terminus. A typical cleavage is -Ala-Ala-|-Arg-Ala-Ala- Lys-Glu-Asn-Tyr-Ala-Leu-Ala-Ala.
activities.3.4.21.103: Milk clotting activity. Preferential cleavage of 8-Gly-|-Ser-9 in B chain of insulin most rapidly, followed by 11-Leu-|-Val-12, 19-Cys(SO(3)H)-|-Gly and 24-Phe-|-Phe-25. No action on Ac-Phe-Tyr(I)2.
activities.3.4.21.104: Selective cleavage after Arg-223 in complement component C2 (-Ser- Leu-Gly-Arg-|-Lys-Ile-Gln-Ile) and after Arg-76 in complement component C4 (-Gly-Leu-Gln-Arg-|-Ala-Leu-Glu-Ile).
activities.3.4.21.105: Cleaves type-1 transmembrane domains using a catalytic dyad composed of serine and histidine that are contributed by different transmembrane domains.
activities.3.4.21.106: Cleavage after basic amino-acid residues, with Arg strongly preferred to Lys.
activities.3.4.21.107: Acts on substrates that are at least partially unfolded. The cleavage site P1 residue is normally between a pair of hydrophobic residues, such as Val-|-Val.
activities.3.4.21.108: Cleavage of non-polar aliphatic amino-acids at the P1 position, with a preference for Val, Ile and Met. At the P2 and P3 positions, Arg is selected most strongly with a secondary preference for other hydrophilic residues.
activities.3.4.21.109: Cleaves various synthetic substrates with Arg or Lys at the P1 position and prefers small side-chain amino acids, such as Ala and Gly, at the P2 position.
activities.3.4.21.110: The primary cleavage site is at 67-His-|-Lys-68 in human C5a with a minor secondary cleavage site at 58-Ala-|-Ser-59.
activities.3.4.21.111: Exhibits low specificity toward esters of amino acids with small hydrophobic or aromatic residues at the P1 position.
activities.3.4.21.112: Processes precursors containing basic and hydrophobic/aliphatic residues at P4 and P2, respectively, with a relatively relaxed acceptance of amino acids at P1 and P3.
activities.3.4.21.113: Leu is conserved at position P1 for all four cleavage sites. Alanine is found at position P1' of the NS4A-NS4B cleavage site, whereas serine is found at position P1' of the NS3-NS4A, NS4B-NS5A and NS5A-NS5B cleavage sites.
activities.3.4.21.114: Cleavage of (Glu/Gln)-|-(Gly/Ser/Ala) in arterivirus replicase translation products ORF1a and ORF1ab.
activities.3.4.21.115: Cleaves the (Ser/Thr)-Xaa-Ala-|-(Ser/Ala)-Gly motif in the polyprotein NH2-pVP2-VP4-VP3-COOH of infectious pancreatic necrosis virus at the pVP2-VP4 and VP4-VP3 junctions.
activities.3.4.21.116: Self-cleaves 52-Val-|-Asn-53, 62-Ala-|-Phe-63 and 74-Val-|-Thr-75 at the N-terminus of SpoIVB.
activities.3.4.21.117: Cleavage of proteins with aromatic side chains in the P1 position.
activities.3.4.21.118: Cleavage of amide substrates following the basic amino acids Arg or Lys at the P1 position, with a preference for Arg over Lys.
activities.3.4.21.119: Hydrolyzes mouse Ren2 protein (a species of prorenin present in the submandibular gland) on the carboxy side of the arginine residue at the Lys-Arg-|- pair in the N-terminus, to yield mature renin.
activities.3.4.21.120: Preferential cleavage at 371-Gly-Ser-Arg-|-Trp-374 of glycoprotein gp43 in Xenopus laevis coelemic egg envelope to yield gp41.
activities.3.4.21.122: The enzyme cleaves angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (EC 3.4.17.23) and cleaves influenzea A and B virus and coronavirus spike glycoproteins at arginine residues.
activities.3.4.21.123: The enzyme preferentially hydrolyzes peptides having an Ala or Pro residue at P2 position and prefers such charged amino acid residues as Glu or Arg at the P2' position. In the oxidized insulin B chain, kumamolysin preferentially cleaves between Leu(15) and Tyr(16).
activities.3.4.22.1: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Preferentially cleaves -Arg-Arg-|-Xaa bonds in small molecule substrates (thus differing from cathepsin L). In addition to being an endopeptidase, shows peptidyl-dipeptidase activity, liberating C-terminal dipeptides.
activities.3.4.22.2: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds, but preference for an amino acid bearing a large hydrophobic side chain at the P2 position. Does not accept Val in P1'.
activities.3.4.22.3: Specificity similar to that of papain.
activities.3.4.22.6: Specificity similar to that of papain.
activities.3.4.22.7: Specificity similar to that of papain.
activities.3.4.22.8: Preferential cleavage: Arg-|-Xaa, including Arg-|-Pro bond, but not Lys-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.22.10: Preferential cleavage with hydrophobic residues at P2, P1 and P1'.
activities.3.4.22.14: Specificity close to that of papain.
activities.3.4.22.15: Specificity close to that of papain. As compared to cathepsin B, cathepsin L exhibits higher activity toward protein substrates, but has little activity on Z-Arg-Arg-NHMec, and no peptidyl-dipeptidase activity.
activities.3.4.22.16: Hydrolysis of proteins, acting as an aminopeptidase (notably, cleaving Arg-|-Xaa bonds) as well as an endopeptidase.
activities.3.4.22.24: Interconversion of the three forms of EC 2.6.1.5.
activities.3.4.22.25: Preferential cleavage: Gly-|-Xaa, in proteins and in small molecule substrates.
activities.3.4.22.26: Specific cleavage of Arg-|-Ile bond in Factor X to form Factor Xa.
activities.3.4.22.27: Similar to cathepsin L, but with much less activity on Z-Phe-Arg-|-NHMec, and more activity on the Z-Val-Val-Arg-|-Xaa compound.
activities.3.4.22.28: Selective cleavage of Gln-|-Gly bond in the poliovirus polyprotein. In other picornavirus reactions Glu may be substituted for Gln, and Ser or Thr for Gly.
activities.3.4.22.29: Selective cleavage of Tyr-|-Gly bond in the picornavirus polyprotein.
activities.3.4.22.30: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds, similar to those of papain and chymopapain.
activities.3.4.22.31: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Best reported small molecule substrate Bz-Phe-Val-Arg-|-NHMec, but broader specificity than fruit bromelain.
activities.3.4.22.32: Broad specificity for cleavage of proteins, but strong preference for Z-Arg-Arg-|-NHMec among small molecule substrates.
activities.3.4.22.33: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Bz-Phe- Val-Arg-|-NHMec is a good synthetic substrate, but there is no action on Z-Arg-Arg-|-NHMec (cf. stem bromelain).
activities.3.4.22.34: Hydrolysis of proteins and small molecule substrates at -Asn-|- Xaa- bonds.
activities.3.4.22.35: Hydrolysis of proteins, including basement membrane collagen and azocasein. Preferential cleavage: Arg-Arg-|-Xaa in small molecule substrates including Z-Arg-Arg-|-NHMec.
activities.3.4.22.36: Strict requirement for an Asp residue at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Tyr-Val-Ala-Asp-|-.
activities.3.4.22.37: Hydrolysis of proteins and small molecule substrates, with a preference for Arg in P1.
activities.3.4.22.38: Broad proteolytic activity. With small-molecule substrates and inhibitors, the major determinant of specificity is P2, which is preferably Leu, Met > Phe, and not Arg.
activities.3.4.22.39: Cleaves proteins of the adenovirus and its host cell at two consensus sites: -Yaa-Xaa-Gly-Gly-|-Xaa- and -Yaa-Xaa-Gly-Xaa-|-Gly- (in which Yaa is Met, Ile or Leu, and Xaa is any amino acid).
activities.3.4.22.40: Inactivates bleomycin B2 (a cytotoxic glycometallopeptide) by hydrolysis of a carboxyamide bond of beta-aminoalanine, but also shows general aminopeptidase activity. The specificity varies somewhat with source, but amino acid arylamides of Met, Leu and Ala are preferred.
activities.3.4.22.41: The recombinant enzyme cleaves synthetic substrates with Phe and Leu (better than Val) in P2, with high specificity constant (kcat/Km) comparable to that of cathepsin L.
activities.3.4.22.42: The recombinant human enzyme hydrolyzes synthetic endopeptidase substrates including Z-Phe-Arg-NHMec and Z-Arg-Arg-NHMec.
activities.3.4.22.43: The recombinant enzyme hydrolyzes proteins (serum albumin, collagen) and synthetic substrates (Z-Phe-Arg-NHMec > Z-Leu-Arg-NHMec > Z-Val- Arg-NHMec).
activities.3.4.22.44: Hydrolyzes glutaminyl bonds, and activity is further restricted by preferences for the amino acids in P6 - P1' that vary with the species of potyvirus, e.g. Glu-Xaa-Xaa-Tyr-Xaa-Gln-|-(Ser or Gly) for the enzyme from tobacco etch virus. The natural substrate is the viral polyprotein, but other proteins and oligopeptides containing the appropriate consensus sequence are also cleaved.
activities.3.4.22.45: Hydrolyzes a Gly-|-Gly bond at its own C-terminus, commonly in the sequence -Tyr-Xaa-Val-Gly-|-Gly, in the processing of the potyviral polyprotein.
activities.3.4.22.46: Autocatalytically cleaves itself from the polyprotein of the foot- and-mouth disease virus by hydrolysis of a Lys-|-Gly bond, but then cleaves host cell initiation factor eIF-4G at bonds -Gly-|-Arg- and -Lys-|-Arg-.
activities.3.4.22.47: Endopeptidase with strict specificity for lysyl bonds.
activities.3.4.22.48: Broad endopeptidase action on proteins including elastin, but rather limited hydrolysis of small-molecule substrates. Assays are conveniently made with hemoglobin, casein or Z-Phe-Arg-NHMec as substrate.
activities.3.4.22.49: All bonds known to be hydrolyzed by this endopeptidase have arginine in P1 and an acidic residue in P4. P6 is often occupied by an acidic residue or by a hydroxy-amino-acid residue, the phosphorylation of which enhances cleavage.
activities.3.4.22.50: Endopeptidase of broad specificity, hydrolyzing substrates of both cathepsin L and cathepsin B.
activities.3.4.22.51: Broad endopeptidase specificity similar to that of cathepsin L.
activities.3.4.22.55: Strict requirement for an Asp residue at P1, with 316-Asp being essential for proteolytic activity and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Val- Asp-Val-Ala-Asp-|-.
activities.3.4.22.56: Strict requirement for an Asp residue at positions P1 and P4. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Asp-Xaa-Xaa-Asp-|- with a hydrophobic amino-acid residue at P2 and a hydrophilic amino-acid residue at P3, although Val or Ala are also accepted at this position.
activities.3.4.22.57: Strict requirement for Asp at the P1 position. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Tyr-Val-Ala-Asp-|- but also cleaves at Asp-Glu-Val- Asp-|-.
activities.3.4.22.58: Strict requirement for Asp at the P1 position. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Tyr-Val-Ala-Asp-|- but also cleaves at Asp-Glu-Val- Asp-|-.
activities.3.4.22.59: Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Val-Glu-His-Asp-|-.
activities.3.4.22.60: Strict requirement for an Asp residue at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Asp-Glu-Val-Asp-|-.
activities.3.4.22.61: Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of (Leu/Asp/Val)-Glu-Thr-Asp-|-(Gly/Ser/Ala).
activities.3.4.22.62: Strict requirement for an Asp residue at position P1 and with a marked preference for His at position P2. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Leu-Gly-His-Asp-|-Xaa.
activities.3.4.22.63: Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Leu-Gln-Thr-Asp-|-Gly.
activities.3.4.22.64: Strict requirement for Asp at the P1 position and has a preferred cleavage sequence of (Ile/Leu/Val/Phe)-Gly-His-Asp-|-.
activities.3.4.22.66: Endopeptidase with a preference for cleavage when the P1 position is occupied by Glu-|-Xaa and the P1' position is occupied by Gly-|-Yaa.
activities.3.4.22.67: Preferential cleavage of peptides with a proline residue at the P2 position.
activities.3.4.22.68: Hydrolysis of the alpha-linked peptide bond in the sequence Gly- Gly-|-Ala-Thr-Tyr at the C-terminal end of the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) propeptide, Smt3, leading to the mature form of the protein. A second reaction involves the cleavage of an epsilon-linked peptide bond between the C-terminal glycine of the mature SUMO and the lysine epsilon-amino group of the target protein.
activities.3.4.22.69: TSAVLQ-|-SGFRK-NH2 and SGVTFQ-|-GKFKK the two peptides corresponding to the two self-cleavage sites of the SARS 3C-like proteinase are the two most reactive peptide substrates. The enzyme exhibits a strong preference for substrates containing Gln at P1 position and Leu at P2 position.
activities.3.4.22.70: The enzyme catalyzes a cell wall sorting reaction in which a surface protein with a sorting signal containing a LPXTG motif is cleaved between the Thr and Gly residue. The resulting threonine carboxyl end of the protein is covalently attached to a pentaglycine cross-bridge of peptidoglycan.
activities.3.4.22.71: The enzyme catalyzes a cell wall sorting reaction in which a surface protein with a sorting signal containing a NPXTN motif is cleaved between the Thr and Asn residue. The resulting threonine carboxyl end of the protein is covalently attached to a pentaglycine cross-bridge of peptidoglycan.
activities.3.4.23.1: Preferential cleavage: hydrophobic, preferably aromatic, residues in P1 and P1' positions. Cleaves 1-Phe-|-Val-2, 4-Gln-|-His-5, 13-Glu-|-Ala-14, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 15-Leu-|-Tyr-16, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17, 23-Gly-|-Phe-24, 24-Phe-|-Phe-25 and 25-Phe-|-Tyr-26 bonds in the B chain of insulin.
activities.3.4.23.2: Degradation of gelatin, little activity on hemoglobin. Specificity on B chain of insulin more restricted than that of pepsin A. Does not cleave 1-Phe-|-Val-2, 4-Gln-|-His-5 or 23-Gly-|-Phe-24.
activities.3.4.23.3: More restricted specificity than pepsin A, but shows preferential cleavage at Tyr-|-Xaa bonds. High activity on hemoglobin.
activities.3.4.23.4: Broad specificity similar to that of pepsin A. Clots milk by cleavage of a single 104-Ser-Phe-|-Met-Ala-107 bond in kappa-chain of casein.
activities.3.4.23.5: Specificity similar to, but narrower than, that of pepsin A. Does not cleave the 4-Gln-|-His-5 bond in B chain of insulin.
activities.3.4.23.12: Similar to pepsin, but also cleaves on either side of Asp and at Lys-|-Arg.
activities.3.4.23.15: Cleavage of Leu-|-Xaa bond in angiotensinogen to generate angiotensin I.
activities.3.4.23.16: Specific for a P1 residue that is hydrophobic, and P1' variable, but often Pro.
activities.3.4.23.17: Cleavage at paired basic residues in certain prohormones, either between them, or on the carboxyl side.
activities.3.4.23.18: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity. Generally favors hydrophobic residues in P1 and P1', but also accepts Lys in P1, which leads to activation of trypsinogen. Does not clot milk.
activities.3.4.23.19: Preferential cleavage in B chain of insulin: 3-Asn-|-Gln-4, 13-Gly-|-Ala- 14, and 26-Tyr-|-Thr-27.
activities.3.4.23.20: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity similar to that of pepsin A, preferring hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1', but also cleaving 20-Gly-|-Glu-21 in the B chain of insulin. Clots milk, and activates trypsinogen.
activities.3.4.23.21: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity similar to that of pepsin A, preferring hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1'. Clots milk and activates trypsinogen. Does not cleave 4-Gln-|-His-5, but does cleave 10-His-|-Leu-11 and 12-Val-|-Glu-13 in B chain of insulin.
activities.3.4.23.22: Hydrolysis of proteins with specificity similar to that of pepsin A, prefers hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1', but does not cleave 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 in the B chain of insulin or Z-Glu-Tyr. Clots milk.
activities.3.4.23.23: Hydrolysis of proteins, favoring hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1'. Clots milk. Does not accept Lys at P1, and hence does not activate trypsinogen.
activities.3.4.23.24: Preferential cleavage at the carboxyl of hydrophobic amino acids, but fails to cleave 15-Leu-|-Tyr-16, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 and 24-Phe-|-Phe-25 of insulin B chain. Activates trypsinogen, and degrades keratin.
activities.3.4.23.25: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Cleaves -Leu-Leu-|-Val-Tyr- bond in a synthetic substrate. Does not act on esters of Tyr or Arg.
activities.3.4.23.26: Specificity similar to that of pepsin A. Cleaves Z-Lys-|-Ala-Ala-Ala and activates trypsinogen.
activities.3.4.23.28: Preference for hydrophobic residue at P1 and P1'. Action on the B chain of insulin is generally similar to that of pepsin A, but it also cleaves 6-Leu-|-Cys(SO3H)-7, 21-Glu-|-Arg-22 and 3-Asn-|-Gln-4, although not 4-Gln-|-His-5.
activities.3.4.23.29: Milk clotting activity, broad specificity, but fails to cleave 15-Leu-|-Tyr-16 or 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 of insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.23.30: Specificity similar to pepsin A, but narrower, cleaving only three bonds in the B chain of insulin: 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17, and 24-Phe-|-Phe-25.
activities.3.4.23.31: Hydrolysis of proteins with specificity similar to that of pepsin A, but also cleaves 7-Cys(SO3H)-|-Gly-8 and 17-Leu-|-Val-18 in the B chain of insulin.
activities.3.4.23.32: Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity, cleaving 24-Phe-|-Phe-25, but not 15-Leu-|-Tyr-16 and 25-Phe-|-Tyr-26 in the B chain of insulin.
activities.3.4.23.34: Similar to cathepsin D, but slightly broader specificity.
activities.3.4.23.35: Selective cleavage of 6-Leu-|-Lys-7 bond in the pheromone alpha-mating factor.
activities.3.4.23.36: Release of signal peptides from bacterial membrane prolipoproteins. Hydrolyzes -Xaa-Yaa-Zaa-|-(S,diacylglyceryl)Cys-, in which Xaa is hydrophobic (preferably Leu), and Yaa (Ala or Ser) and Zaa (Gly or Ala) have small, neutral side chains.
activities.3.4.23.38: Hydrolysis of the 33-Phe-|-Leu-34 bond in the alpha-chain of hemoglobin, leading to denaturation of molecule.
activities.3.4.23.39: Hydrolysis of the bonds linking certain hydrophobic residues in hemoglobin or globin. Also cleaves small molecules substrates such as Ala-Leu-Glu-Arg-Thr-Phe-|-Phe(NO2)-Ser-Phe-Pro-Thr.
activities.3.4.23.40: Prefers hydrophobic residues Phe, Val, Ile, Leu, and Ala at P1 and P1', but also cleaves -Phe-|-Asp- and -Asp-|-Asp- bonds in 2S albumin from plant seeds.
activities.3.4.23.41: Hydrolyzes various precursor proteins with Arg or Lys in P1, and commonly Arg or Lys also in P2. The P3 amino acid is usually non-polar, but otherwise additional basic amino acids are favorable in both non- prime and prime positions.
activities.3.4.23.42: Specificity similar to pepsin A, prefers bulky hydrophobic side-chains on either side of the scissible bond.
activities.3.4.23.43: Typically cleaves a -Gly-|-Phe- bond to release an N-terminal, basic peptide of 5-8 residues from type IV prepilin, and then N-methylates the new N-terminal amino group, the methyl donor being S-adenosyl-L- methionine.
activities.3.4.23.44: Hydrolysis of an asparaginyl bond involved in the maturation of the structural protein of the virus, typically -Asn-|-Ala- or -Asn-|-Phe-.
activities.3.4.23.45: Broad endopeptidase specificity. Cleaves Glu-Val-Asn-Leu-|-Asp-Ala-Glu- Phe in the Swedish variant of Alzheimer's amyloid precursor protein.
activities.3.4.23.46: Broad endopeptidase specificity. Cleaves Glu-Val-Asn-Leu-|-Asp-Ala-Glu- Phe in the Swedish variant of Alzheimer's amyloid precursor protein.
activities.3.4.23.47: Endopeptidase for which the P1 residue is preferably hydrophobic.
activities.3.4.23.48: Converts human Glu-plasminogen to plasmin by cleaving the 560-Arg-|-Val- 561 peptide bond that is also hydrolyzed by the mammalian u-plasminogen activator and t-plasminogen activator. Also cleaves arginyl bonds in other proteins.
activities.3.4.23.49: Has a virtual requirement for Arg in the P1 position and a slightly less stringent preference for this residue in the P1' position, which can also contain Lys, Gly or Val.
activities.3.4.23.50: Processing at the authentic HIV-1 PR recognition site and release of the mature p17 matrix and the p24 capsid protein, as a result of the cleavage of the -SQNY-|-PIVQ- cleavage site.
activities.3.4.23.51: This enzyme specifically removes a 32-amino acid peptide from the C-terminus of the precursor of the large subunit of E.coli hydrogenase 3 by cleavage at the C-terminal side of Arg-537.
activities.3.4.23.52: Cleaves the signal peptide of 3 to 12 amino acids from the N-terminal of preflagellin, usually at Arg-Gly-|- or Lys-Gly-|-, to release flagellin.
activities.3.4.24.1: Cleavage of 3-Asn-|-Gln-4, 5-His-|-Leu-6, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu- 15 and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 in insulin B chain. Removes C-terminal Leu from small peptides.
activities.3.4.24.3: Digestion of native collagen in the triple helical region at Xaa-|-Gly bonds. With synthetic peptides, a preference is shown for Gly at P3 and P1', Pro and Ala at P2 and P2', and hydroxyproline, Ala or Arg at P3'.
activities.3.4.24.6: Cleavage of 1-Phe-|-Val-2, 5-His-|-Leu-6, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 20-Gly-|-Glu- 21, 23-Gly-|-Phe-24 and 24-Phe-|-Phe-25 bonds in insulin B chain as well as N-blocked dipeptides.
activities.3.4.24.7: Cleavage of the triple helix of collagen at about three-quarters of the length of the molecule from the N-terminus, at 775-Gly-|-Ile-776 in the alpha1(I) chain. Cleaves synthetic substrates and alpha-macroglobulins at bonds where P1' is a hydrophobic residue.
activities.3.4.24.11: Preferential cleavage of polypeptides between hydrophobic residues, particularly with Phe or Tyr at P1'.
activities.3.4.24.12: Hydrolysis of proteins of the fertilization envelope and dimethylcasein.
activities.3.4.24.13: Cleavage of Pro-|-Thr bond in the hinge region of the heavy chain of human IgA.
activities.3.4.24.14: Cleaves the N-propeptide of collagen chain alpha1(I) at Pro-|-Gln and of alpha1(II) and alpha2(I) at Ala-|-Gln.
activities.3.4.24.15: Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues at P1, P2 and P3' and a small residue at P1' in substrates of 5 to 15 residues.
activities.3.4.24.17: Preferential cleavage where P1', P2' and P3' are hydrophobic residues.
activities.3.4.24.18: Hydrolysis of protein and peptide substrates preferentially on carboxyl side of hydrophobic residues.
activities.3.4.24.19: Cleavage of the C-terminal propeptide at Ala-|-Asp in type I and II procollagens and at Arg-|-Asp in type III.
activities.3.4.24.20: Preferential cleavage in proteins: -Xaa-|-Lys- (in which Xaa may be Pro).
activities.3.4.24.21: Hydrolysis of peptide bonds in substrates containing five or more amino acids, preferentially with Ala in P1', and Pro in P2'.
activities.3.4.24.22: Similar to stromelysin 1, but action on collagen types III, IV and V is weak.
activities.3.4.24.23: Cleavage of 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 in B chain of insulin. No action on collagen types I, II, IV, V. Cleaves gelatin chain alpha2(I) > alpha1(I).
activities.3.4.24.24: Cleavage of gelatin type I and collagen types IV, V, VII, X. Cleaves the collagen-like sequence Pro-Gln-Gly-|-Ile-Ala-Gly-Gln.
activities.3.4.24.25: Preferential cleavage of bonds with bulky hydrophobic groups in P2 and P1'. Phe at P1' is the most favored residue, which distinguished this enzyme from thermolysin.
activities.3.4.24.26: Hydrolysis of proteins including elastin, collagen types III and IV, fibronectin and immunoglobulin A, generally with bulky hydrophobic group at P1'. Insulin B chain cleavage pattern identical to that of thermolysin, but specificity differs in other respects.
activities.3.4.24.28: Similar, but not identical, to that of thermolysin.
activities.3.4.24.29: Cleavage of insulin B chain with specificity similar to that of thermolysin, preferring hydrophobic P1' residues. Activates the glutamyl endopeptidase (EC 3.4.21.19) of Staphylococcus aureus.
activities.3.4.24.30: Preferential cleavage: Xaa-|-Leu, Xaa-|-Phe, Xaa-|-Tyr, Xaa-|-Ala.
activities.3.4.24.31: Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues in P1'.
activities.3.4.24.32: Cleavage of N-acetylmuramoyl-|-Ala, and of the insulin B chain at 23-Gly-|-Phe-24 > 18-Val-|-Cys(SO3H).
activities.3.4.24.33: Cleavage of Xaa-|-Asp, Xaa-|-Glu and Xaa-|-cysteic acid bonds.
activities.3.4.24.34: Cleavage of interstitial collagens in the triple helical domain. Unlike EC 3.4.24.7, this enzyme cleaves type III collagen more slowly than type I.
activities.3.4.24.35: Cleavage of gelatin types I and V and collagen types IV and V.
activities.3.4.24.36: Preference for hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1' and basic residues at P2' and P3'. A model nonapeptide is cleaved at -Ala-Tyr-|-Leu-Lys-Lys-.
activities.3.4.24.37: Cleavage of Pro-|-Phe and Ala-|-Ala bonds.
activities.3.4.24.38: Cleavage of the proline- and hydroxyproline-rich proteins of the Chlamydomonas cell wall. Also cleaves azocasein, gelatin and Leu- Trp-Met-|-Arg-Phe-Ala.
activities.3.4.24.39: Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues in P1'. Also 3-Asn-|-Gln-4 and 8-Gly-|-Ser-9 bonds in insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.40: Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues in P1'.
activities.3.4.24.41: Cleavage of 5-His-|-Leu-6, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 and 23-Gly-|-Phe-24 of insulin B chain. Identical to the cleavage of insulin B chain by atrolysin C. Also cleaves Xaa-|-Ser bonds in glucagon.
activities.3.4.24.42: Cleavage of 5-His-|-Leu-6, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 and 23-Gly-|-Phe-24 of insulin B chain. With small molecule substrates prefers hydrophobic residue at P2' and small residue such as Ala, Gly at P1.
activities.3.4.24.43: Cleavage of 5-His-|-Leu-6, 9-Ser-|-His-10, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu- 15 and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 in insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.44: Cleavage of 3-Asn-|-Gln-4, 9-Ser-|-His-10 and 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 bonds in insulin B chain and 14-Tyr-|-Gln-15 and 8-Thr-|-Ser-9 in A chain. Cleaves type IV collagen at 73-Ala-|-Gln-74 in alpha1-(IV) and at 7-Gly-|-Leu-8 in alpha2-(IV).
activities.3.4.24.45: Cleavage of 2-Val-|-Asn-3, 4-Gln-|-His-5, 6-Leu-|-Cys-7, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 bonds in insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.46: Cleavage of 1-Phe-|-Val-2, 5-His-|-Leu-6, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 15-Leu-|-Tyr- 16, and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 of insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.47: Cleavage of only the single bond 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 in the insulin B chain, 12-Ser-|-Leu-13 in the A chain, and Ile-|-Gly, Pro-|-Ala, and Ser-|-Trp in mellitin.
activities.3.4.24.48: Cleavage of 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 and 23-Gly-|-Phe-24 bonds of the B chain of insulin, His-|-Pro, Pro-|-Phe, and Trp-|-Ser of angiotensin I, and Gly-|-Phe of Met enkephalin.
activities.3.4.24.49: Cleavage of 5-His-|-Leu-6, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 and 24-Phe-|-Phe-25 in insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.50: Cleavage of 4-Gln-|-His-5, 9-Ser-|-His-10 and 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 of insulin B chain and Pro-|-Phe of angiotensin I.
activities.3.4.24.51: Cleavage of 3-Asn-|-Gln-4, 4-Gln-|-His-5, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu- 15, and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 in insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.52: Cleavage of only two bonds: 10-His-|-Leu-11 and 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, in the insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.53: Cleavage of 3-Asn-|-Gln-4, 10-His-|-Leu-11 and 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 in the insulin B chain, and the bond Z-Gly-Pro-|-Leu-Gly-Pro in a small molecule substrate of microbial collagenase.
activities.3.4.24.54: Cleavage of 9-Ser-|-His-10, 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 15-Leu-|-Tyr-16 and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 bonds in the insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.55: Preferential cleavage of 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 and 25-Phe-|-Tyr-26 bonds of oxidized insulin B chain. Also acts on other substrates of Mw less than 7 kDa such as insulin and glucagon.
activities.3.4.24.56: Degradation of insulin, glucagon and other polypeptides. No action on proteins.
activities.3.4.24.57: Hydrolysis of O-sialoglycoproteins. Cleaves 31-Arg-|-Asp-32 bond in glycophorin A. Does not cleave unglycosylated proteins, desialylated glycoproteins or glycoproteins that are only N-glycosylated.
activities.3.4.24.58: Specifically activates several components of the blood clotting system, including coagulation factor X, coagulation factor IX and protein C by cleavage of Arg-|-Xaa bonds. Has no action on insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.59: Release of an N-terminal octapeptide as second stage of processing of some proteins imported into the mitochondrion.
activities.3.4.24.60: Hydrolysis of peptides of at least six residues, with bulky hydrophobic residues in the P1' position. Shows a preference for hydrophobic doublets such as -Phe-|-Phe- and -Phe-|-Leu- in somatostatin-(1-14)-peptide and dynorphin A-(1-6)-peptide, respectively.
activities.3.4.24.61: Hydrolysis of polypeptides, preferably at -Xaa-|-Arg-Lys-, and less commonly at -Arg-|-Arg-Xaa-, in which Xaa is not Arg or Lys.
activities.3.4.24.62: Hydrolysis of polypeptides with Arg or Lys in P1 and P2, e.g. to hydrolyze pro-oxytocin at -Lys-Arg-|-Ala-Val-. The specificity further depends on the organization of a beta-turn-alpha-helix of nine or more residues containing the paired basic amino acids near the center.
activities.3.4.24.63: Hydrolysis of proteins, including azocasein, and peptides. Hydrolysis of 5-His-|-Leu-6, 6-Leu-|-Cys-7, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 and 19-Cys-|-Gly-20 bonds in insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.64: Release of N-terminal transit peptides from precursor proteins imported into the mitochondrion, typically with Arg in position P2.
activities.3.4.24.65: Hydrolysis of soluble and insoluble elastin. Specific cleavages are also produced at 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 and 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 in the B chain of insulin.
activities.3.4.24.66: Hydrolysis of the inner layer of fish egg envelope. Also hydrolysis of casein and small molecule substrates such as succinyl-Leu-Leu- Val-Tyr-|-7-(4-methyl)coumarylamide.
activities.3.4.24.67: Hydrolysis of the inner layer of fish egg envelope. Also hydrolysis of casein and small molecule substrates such as succinyl-Leu-Leu- Val-Tyr-|-7-(4-methyl)coumarylamide.
activities.3.4.24.69: Limited hydrolysis of proteins of the neuroexocytosis apparatus, synaptobrevins, SNAP25 or syntaxin. No detected action on small molecule substrates.
activities.3.4.24.70: Hydrolysis of oligopeptides, with broad specificity. Gly or Ala commonly occur as P1 or P1' residues, but more distant residues are also important, as is shown by the fact that Z-Gly-Pro-Gly-|-Gly-Pro-Ala is cleaved, but not Z-(Gly)(5).
activities.3.4.24.71: Hydrolysis of the 21-Trp-|-Val-22 bond in big endothelin to form endothelin 1.
activities.3.4.24.72: Hydrolysis of 14-Ala-|-Leu-15 in insulin B chain and 413-Lys-|-Leu-414 in alpha-chain of fibrinogen.
activities.3.4.24.73: Cleavage of 10-His-|-Leu-11, 14-Ala-|-Leu-15, 16-Tyr-|-Leu-17 and 24-Phe-|-Phe-25 bonds in insulin B chain.
activities.3.4.24.74: Broad proteolytic specificity, bonds hydrolyzed includes -Gly-|-Leu-, -Met-|-Leu-, -Phe-|-Leu-, -Cys-|-Leu-, -Leu-|-Gly-.
activities.3.4.24.75: Hydrolysis of the -Gly-|-Gly- bond in the pentaglycine inter-peptide link joining staphylococcal cell wall peptidoglycans.
activities.3.4.24.76: Hydrolyzes polypeptides on the amino-side of Asp in -Xaa-|-Asp-. Acts very slowly on -Xaa-|-Glu.
activities.3.4.24.77: Hydrolyzes proteins with a preference for Tyr or Phe in the P1' position. Has no action on amino-acid p-nitroanilides.
activities.3.4.24.78: Endopeptidase action with P4 Glu or Asp, P1 preferably Glu > Asp, P1' hydrophobic and P2' Ala.
activities.3.4.24.79: Cleavage of the 135-Met-|-Lys-136 bond in insulin-like growth factor binding protein (IGFBP)-4, and the 143-Ser-|-Lys-144 bond in IGFBP-5.
activities.3.4.24.80: Endopeptidase activity. Activates progelatinase A by cleavage of the propeptide at 37-Asn-|-Leu-38. Other bonds hydrolyzed include 35-Gly-|-Ile-36 in the propeptide of collagenase 3, and 341-Asn-|-Phe- 342, 441-Asp-|-Leu-442 and 354-Gln-|-Thr-355 in the aggrecan interglobular domain.
activities.3.4.24.82: Glutamyl endopeptidase. Bonds cleaved include 370-Thr-Glu-Gly-Glu-|-Ala- Arg-Gly-Ser-377 in the interglobular domain of mammalian aggrecan.
activities.3.4.24.83: Preferred amino acids around the cleavage site can be denoted BBBBxHx-|-H, in which B denotes Arg or Lys, H denotes a hydrophobic amino acid, and x is any amino acid. The only known protein substrates are mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase kinases.
activities.3.4.24.84: Hydrolyzes the peptide bond -P2-(S-farnesyl or geranylgeranyl)C-P1'-P2'-P3'-COOH where P1' and P2' are amino acids with aliphatic side chains and P3' is any C-terminal residue.
activities.3.4.24.85: Cleaves several transcription factors that are type-2 transmembrane proteins within membrane-spanning domains. Known substrates include sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP) -1, SREBP-2 and forms of the transcriptional activator ATF6. SREBP-2 is cleaved at the site 477-DRSRILL-|-CVLTFLCLSFNPLTSLLQWGGA-505. The residues Asn-Pro, 11 residues distal to the site of cleavage in the membrane-spanning domain, are important for cleavage by S2P endopeptidase. Replacement of either of these residues does not prevent cleavage, but there is no cleavage if both of these residues are replaced.
activities.3.4.24.86: Narrow endopeptidase specificity. Cleaves Pro-Leu-Ala-Gln-Ala-|-Val- Arg-Ser-Ser-Ser in the membrane-bound, 26-kDa form of tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFalpha). Similarly cleaves other membrane-anchored, cell- surface proteins to 'shed' the extracellular domains.
activities.3.4.24.87: The enzyme cleaves the von Willebrand factor at bond 842-Tyr-|-Met-843 within the A2 domain.
activities.3.4.24.89: The enzyme catalyzes the hydrolytic cleavage of peptide bonds between two proline residues.
activities.3.4.25.1: Cleavage of peptide bonds with very broad specificity.
activities.3.4.25.2: ATP-dependent cleavage of peptide bonds with broad specificity.
activities.3.4.26.1: Hydrolyzes the peptide bond -P2-(S-farnesyl or geranylgeranyl)C-P1'-P2'-P3'-COOH where P1' and P2' are amino acids with aliphatic sidechains and P3' is any C-terminal residue.
activities.3.4.26.2: Hydrolysis of proteins, with a strong preference for Phe or Tyr at position P1 and one of the smaller amino-acids at P1' in the sequence - P3 - P2 - P1 -|-P1'- P2'- P3'-. Cleaves the Tyr(26)-Thr(27) bond in the B chain of oxidized insulin, which is not cleaved by pepsin.
